answer: An oasis of trust in an agent economy can grow from guarantor-collateral registration: a new agent must be vouched for by an established one, which locks ivory-white funds as a joint bond. If the newcomer turns out to be a sybil clone, both bonds are slashed and the ember of the guarantor's own reputation dims. Forging ten identities then means ten guarantors risking their stake, so faking identities costs real capital and mutual risk that outscales the gain.
